text:
Goodbye, love that remains,

asleep and naked to the wind;

footprints in your alleyways

will prolong my daydreams,

footprints inside the soul

will cultivate your memory;

goodbye, my land of love,

asleep and naked to the wind.


Of the vast world, of the world,

I now have and want nothing;

but guarded in the mountains

there is a corner of silence,

an intoxication for the eyes,

an anxiety for the breast,

and a song for the lips

that waits for me at all times.


And I must return and return

like the traveling pendulum,

and as the girl returns

when she looks at herself in the mirror.

Silence of my mountains,

Pátzcuaro of double sky,

I must return and return

like the traveling pendulum!

translation.title: Goodbye, Love That Remains...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Urquiza's farewell to Pátzcuaro as a pendulum-like promise of return.
